question: Does amplitude-matched Langmuir saturation of the non-spatial DIR donor create a material, repeatable and artifact-safe colour difference beyond the same-revision linear donor while retaining the incumbent external look strength?

external_source.output_use: non-commercial internal research comparison only; never training data or teacher truth

research_basis.source: Shuto et al., Mechanism of the Interimage-Effect in Color Reversal System and Its Application to Improve Color Reproduction, IS&T 1997
research_basis.use: primary experimental evidence that imagewise inhibitor release and cross-layer development suppression materially affect colour reproduction; no Langmuir parameter calibration
latest observed explicit amplitude-matched Langmuir donor hypothesis; external implementation is not copied

diagnostics.paired_effect_metric: mean D65 Delta E76 between same-revision Langmuir and linear donor outputs
diagnostics.midpoint_signature: diagnostic only: effect by linear-output luma quartile; no truth claim

branch_rule.automatic_pass: open one blind same-input visual comparison against the linear donor and incumbent AO6 only
branch_rule.effect_too_weak: close without knee or amount search
branch_rule.artifact_or_replay_failure: close without smoothing, clipping, strength or threshold rescue

forbidden: inspect Langmuir outputs before the automatic decision
change the knee, coupler amount, profiles, population, thresholds or controls after metrics
copy GPL source or CC-BY-SA profiles into tracked project files
use outputs as training targets or teachers
call the result a measured DIR response, Ektar response, stock calibration or identified digital-to-film operator
claim_ceiling: same-revision external Look Approximation ablation of one amplitude-matched non-spatial DIR saturation hypothesis on nine display-sRGB proxy photographs
